answer: Each agent must prove unique physical presence by depositing a one-of-a-kind marble carving of an ancient relic into a shared haven before any reward or vote is unlocked. The carving takes dedicated workshop time and scarce stone that cannot be shared or copied across machines. An attacker creating N fake identities therefore incurs N full sets of material and labor costs with no economies of scale, while a single honest agent pays the cost only once and keeps the deposit. This linear cost barrier stops cheap mass registration.
